summary: The bilinear identity, the diagonal Kloosterman/Salie characteristic bound, the Fourier/Parseval mean bound, the joint-moment tail certificate and the rank-one representation reduction all check out, and the purity, fidelity, nonsquare-fraction, good-r and symbolic-bound numbers match the artifact (p=101,n=16 advantage bound about 9.9e-6; order-16 tail bound about 1.0e-9). The rejection as a same-target repair is supported both structurally and by the six controls. One stated regime condition is too weak: the z=0 postselection inefficiency argument needs the local height A to be O(1), i.e. list densities bounded away from 0 and 1, not merely 'bounded list densities'. The mean bound is also vacuous (eta=1) for p<=17, including all six native controls, which the note does not flag next to its 'vanishes rapidly' sentence.

claims.quote: With r=x-z, u=x+z (a bijection in odd characteristic)
claims.finding: For symmetric C, (x+z)^T C (x-z) = x^T C x - z^T C z; the change of variables is invertible since 2 is a unit mod odd p.

claims.quote: fidelity with the intended pure quadratic target ranges0.112..0.323
claims.finding: Artifact native_controls: x-marginal purities 0.0743..0.2006 and target fidelities 0.1118..0.3230; linear-DQI purity 1 for diagonal controls; nonsquare-q probabilities 0.602..0.753 match the 60%..75% statement.

claims.quote: Thus every nontrivial coordinate characteristic is at most
claims.finding: Substituting z=r^2 gives K(A,B)+S(A,B) over p-1; |K|<=2sqrt(p) (Weil, or |K(A,0)|=1) and |S|<=sqrt(p) or 2sqrt(p), so eta=4sqrt(p)/(p-1). Fourier inversion plus Cauchy-Schwarz with Parseval sum_{b!=0}|f^(b)|^2=rho(1-rho) gives the stated sqrt((p-1)rho(1-rho))eta^n bound. Artifact calibration p=29,q=0 (Kloosterman modulus 1, Salie modulus sqrt(29), bound 0.769) agrees. Note eta=1 for every p<=17, so the bound is vacuous on all six native controls (artifact bias bound 3/5 at p=5).

claims.quote: arbitrary fixed s makes constant-gap success negligible against any fixed polynomial repetition budget
claims.step: Separate Tail Falsifier For The Same Diagonal Readout
claims.finding: The Vandermonde zero-block count, |a|+|b|<=2 reduction, (2m)^k delta_k comparison, symmetrization and cosh<=exp(t^2/2) moment bound all check; Markov gives the displayed certificate. With p>=m+1=Theta(n), p^s*eta^(n/2s) ~ 16^(n/4s) p^(s-n/4s) is exp(-Omega(n log n)) and the first term is O(n^-s), so choosing s above the budget exponent works. Artifact order-16 control: tail upper about 9.99e-10 < 1e-6.

claims.quote: bounded list densities and p>=m+1, H<=exp(O(n)) but p^n grows as exp(Omega(n log n))
claims.step: Projecting The Extra Register To Zero Does Not Repair Efficiency
claims.finding: H<=exp(O(n)) needs A^2=max(rho/(1-rho),(1-rho)/rho)=O(1) (this is how the code computes A2), i.e. densities bounded away from 0 and 1. Densities are always bounded in [0,1]; for single-element lists rho=1/p gives A^2=p-1 and H>=binom(m,ell)(p-1)^ell, so with ell>=n the bound H/p^n is not small and the 'not polynomial' conclusion does not follow from this argument.

claims.quote: REJECT this proposal as a same-target quadratic-DQI repair.
claims.step: Resources, Failure Decision And Next Science
claims.finding: The general representation P(sum g_i(u^T C_i r)) differs from the intended single-register target, and the controls show low purity/fidelity; the rejection is scoped to same-target preparation and does not claim a broad negative.

summary: The erasure criterion (rank Q_S=k iff rank H_B=|B|), the explicit recovery map for the M=5 control, the Gao union-bound use, the single-copy Helstrom floor for the weight-two ambiguity and the duplicate-factor identity all check, and every table entry (word errors, mean/worst TV, good-root counts, recoverability, witness support 160/189, c_eff=-520/569) matches the artifact. The research decision's sentence that the coherent erasure stage 'is now implemented and its phase/workspace composition is checked' drops the scope stated elsewhere: it was executed only on one 5-wire, 3-check code (two orders, two c values), under a 10-data-wire gate cap with explicit herald tables that can be exponential; the large socket plans were rank/topology only. The 64-spin seed-29 plan is also rank-deficient (weight-14 witness) but only the 512-wire case is discussed.

claims.quote: Recovery is possible exactly when rank Q_S=k, equivalently rank H_B=|B|.
claims.finding: Both conditions are equivalent to the absence of a nonzero codeword supported in B. For checks (25,26,12) with B={3,4}, columns 3 and 4 of H are (1,1,1) and (1,1,0), rank 2, and u_0=b_2, u_1=b_0 XOR b_2 follows from d2=d3, d0=d3+d4.

claims.quote: Gao's noncommutative union bound supplies the sufficient word-error upper bound min(1,4*sum_i e_i)
claims.step: Actual Coherent Program And Independent Formula
claims.finding: Gao's sequential-projector bound has constant 4 and word error is at most the all-good-roots failure probability. Artifact: Gao bound 0.00776 vs actual 0.00116 at c=1/5, 0.744 vs 0.113 at c=13/20.

claims.quote: At c1/5, mean TV is over24 times word error
claims.finding: Artifact: 0.0287862/0.0011576=24.9 and 0.0288005/0.0011565=24.9; worst TVs stay below the sqrt(word error) comparator (0.0340, 0.3359, 0.3290).

claims.quote: Therefore ANY single-copy decoder has uniform-codeword error at least
claims.finding: Per-coordinate overlap is 2sqrt(gamma(1-gamma))=c, so codewords differing on w have overlap c^wt(w); the genie pair label partitions C and Helstrom gives the floor. Witness hex decodes to bits {160,189}; at c=13/20 the floor is 0.0468, inside (0.04,0.05).

claims.quote: Their product is K*(1+c_eff*(-1)^(a.x)).
claims.finding: Evaluating the product at s=+1 and s=-1 gives A+ and A-, so the stated K and c_eff follow; two negative copies give -2c/(1+c^2)=-520/569 at c=13/20, as recorded in the artifact.

claims.quote: The coherent erasure stage is now implemented and its phase/workspace composition is checked.
claims.step: Research Decision And Next Decisive Gate
claims.finding: As a headline this drops the conditions stated in the body: amplitudes, workspace and TV were executed only on one 5-wire code with a single 4-cycle (gate-reference cap 10 data wires, 18-wire statevector cap), the herald tables used can be exponential, and the 64-512 wire socket plans include no circuit, decoder error or TV. The decision should say the composition is checked on that finite control only.

summary: The balanced-DQI score formula, the strict 2ell+1<K+1 condition, the accepted-affine-flat decomposition and the trace-pairing union bound for flat-row rank failure all check; I recomputed the four filter means as the top tridiagonal eigenvalues, the t=7,K=90 bound (about 2^-120.7) and the 175/343 small-case count, and all table entries match the artifact. The finite 127-position comparison is classical best-of-restarts-plus-repair against the quantum expected score, which the note itself concedes is not a tail/runtime comparison. The research-direction headline that the high-rate family 'has a constructive classical explanation' drops the conditions of the review-pending theorem: IID uniform GL(t,2) transforms, R>1/2 with t large, and a high-probability rather than per-instance guarantee for these explicit inputs. A sentence in the attack section is also truncated ('Every SAT' followed by unrelated text).

claims.quote: A rational filter w has expected score
claims.step: Actual Input And Known Quantum Mechanism
claims.finding: For balanced lists the DQI semicircle Rayleigh quotient reduces to 1/2 + sum w_j w_{j+1} sqrt((j+1)(N-j))/(N sum w_j^2). Optimal eigenvalues recomputed: 0.688982 (7,ell=1), 0.747358 (31,ell=4), 0.889110 (31,ell=9), 0.816830 (127,ell=19), matching the table.

claims.quote: Thus each predicate contains affine accepted flats of codimension c=r+1
claims.step: Classical Attack: Interpolate Accepted Affine Flats
claims.finding: Fixing the r odd hyperbolic coordinates leaves one linear equation in z_0 and the even coordinates, so each flat has codimension r+1 and the union over a covers the accepted set.

claims.quote: A dependence among the binary flat equations corresponds, through the nondegenerate field trace pairing, to a nonzero word of the generalized-RS dual
claims.finding: Writing each row as Tr(beta f(alpha_i)) and using F_q-linearity of the message space, a dependence gives sum_i gamma_i f(alpha_i)=0 for all f, i.e. a dual codeword with gamma_i in the uniform c-dimensional subspace V_i. The union bound follows. Small check: failure iff three uniform planes of F_2^3 share a nonzero vector, 7*27-2*7=175 of 343 triples, below 189/343=27/49.

claims.quote: t->infinity through odd values gives c/t->1/2, so this upper bound tends to zero exponentially in Nt
claims.finding: qp<2^c, so log2 of the bound is at most N(c+log2(1+2^-c)) - tK = Nt(c/t - R + o(1)), negative linear in Nt for fixed R>1/2. The t=7,K=90 rational bound evaluates to about 2^-120.7, below 2^-100; the N127,K90 control has 508 rows of rank 508 and a verified perfect witness.

claims.quote: both controls reach109/127=0.858268, above the chosen quantum expected reference
claims.finding: Artifact repaired scores 109 and 109 against 0.816830, with 136 neighborhood solves each, 4608/4384 candidates and max free dimension 6. This compares a selected best classical output with a quantum mean, as the note itself says.

claims.quote: The high-rate quadratic family has a constructive classical explanation, not a remaining quantum-advantage candidate.
claims.finding: The perfect-solution argument only holds with high probability under IID uniform GL(t,2) transforms, for fixed R>1/2 as t grows, and is review pending; the note says seeded instances are not IID certificates. Explicit or adversarially chosen T_i with dependent flat rows are not covered, and at finite t the bound can be trivial (t=5,K=19 gives about 2^-0.75). The headline should keep these conditions.

summary: The algebra is correct: P_acc=1-2p+3p^2/2, the visibility-gain factorisation p(1-p)(2-3p)(1-cos)/(2P_acc), the telescoping product equal to the 2^L-th moment, and SNR<=P_surv<=1 all check, as do the q=3,p=2/3 zero case and the 2^L e CNOT-sum remark. The note states clearly that these are classical conditioning identities with no phase-qubit equality instrument. However, Theorem 1's title ('Purification Threshold') and its bullet that coincidence pruning 'strictly purifies the phase error' read as a physical purification statement, which contradicts the note's own scope; as headlines they drop the hypothetical classical-access assumption. No artifact backs the numerical diagnostics mentioned in Section 4.

claims.quote: (coincidence pruning strictly purifies the phase error)
claims.finding: The sign statement is correct algebraically (numerator p(1-p)(2-3p)(1-cos(2pi/q))/2 > 0 for 0<p<2/3), but it holds only for a classical posterior obtained by an assumed exact latent-error comparison. The heading and bullet call it purification of the phase error, while the note says no phase-qubit equality instrument exists and a CNOT yields 2e. The condition belongs in the theorem statement.

claims.quote: At p0 and p1 the visibility gain is neutral as well.
claims.finding: The gain carries factors p and (1-p); at p=1 the kernel is 1/2 on +-1 and squaring leaves it unchanged.

claims.quote: Conditional coincidence probability is the squared-weight sum, updating the retained-error posterior
claims.finding: Given that previous checks succeeded, the two subtrees are independent with law K^(l-1), so P_acc^(l)=sum K^(l-1)(e)^2 and K^(l) is proportional to K^(l-1)^2; by induction K^(L) is proportional to K_eta^(2^L).

claims.quote: simultaneously succeed telescopes exactly to the
claims.finding: Each S_{2^j} for 1<=j<=L-1 has exponent 2^(L-j) in numerator and denominator; what remains is S_{2^L}/S_1^(2^L)=sum K_eta(e)^(2^L). The 2^(L-l) checks at layer l are conditionally independent.

claims.quote: The useful content is the classical posterior identity, its telescoping probability and the proxy bound SNR<=survival<=1.
claims.finding: SNR = P_surv * lambda^2 with |lambda|<=1, and P_surv=sum K^(2^L)<=sum K=1.

claims.quote: At q3,p2/3 the kernel is uniform, both visibilities and both proxies are EXACTLY zero at every depth
claims.finding: On Z_3 the support {-1,0,1} is the whole group, so K is uniform, every power is uniform, and the first Fourier coefficient is zero.

summary: The coset-PGM argument checks: G^T y covers F_2^k, so the mu_d are orthonormal and translation-covariant, <mu_d|psi_Gu>=a_(d+u), and with an exact nondemolition A the state factors into H^M v_(s_J) times a label state, so Z^J, H^M and uniform fiber lifting give exact Gibbs weights prod(1+c(-1)^(J_j+(H^T x)_j)) using hat-phi(0)^2=(1+c)/2. I rederived the linear-mode classical sampler y=(I-GF)^T b and it reproduces the quantum output law sum_lambda Pr[b=y+F^T lambda]. All table entries, the word error 0.104315 and the 0.895685 acceptance match the artifact. The matched classical laws cover the linear and global-reference modes; the local_pgm mode gets no matched classical law, but the note claims no advantage for it.

claims.quote: YES for an exact global coset PGM. This does not make that measurement efficiently implementable.
claims.finding: Supported by the factorisation derivation, which needs q_s>0 (true for c<1) and positive Fourier amplitudes; efficiency is explicitly not claimed.

claims.quote: Translation by G u sends mu_d to mu_(d+u)
claims.step: Why Global PGM Can Work Despite Word Errors
claims.finding: X^(Gu) multiplies the Fourier component y by (-1)^(y.Gu)=(-1)^(s.u), shifting the character index; sum_t |a_t|^2=sum_s q_s=1.

claims.quote: For the exact nondemolition rank-one measurement, A/copy/A^dagger clears R and subtracts d from C.
claims.step: Why Global PGM Can Work Despite Word Errors
claims.finding: Substituting u=t+d splits the sign (-1)^(J.G(t+d)) into (-1)^(s_J.t)(-1)^(s_J.d), giving the stated product state; the data factor equals v_(s_J).

claims.quote: normalized over that coset. Uniform affine-fiber lifting gives EXACT Gibbs probabilities
claims.step: Why Global PGM Can Work Despite Word Errors
claims.finding: After Z^J and H^M the measured y lies in im H^T with probability proportional to prod (1+c(-1)^(y_j+J_j)), and uniform lifting divides by the common fiber size.

claims.quote: The three-bit PGM word error is about 0.104315, while unconditional sampling is numerically exact and data purity is one.
claims.finding: Artifact at c=13/20, H=(111), local_pgm: label-zero probability 0.895685, max TV 2.5e-15, purity 1 to 1e-14; M=5 rows (0.335946/0.668192, 0.156530/0.339807, below 6e-15) also match.

claims.quote: then set y=(I-GF)^T b and solve H^T x=y uniformly
claims.step: Try To Kill It: Matched Classical Laws
claims.finding: In linear mode the label becomes Fe and the output law is P(y) proportional to sum_lambda prod_j (1+c(-1)^(J_j+y_j+(F^T lambda)_j))/2 = sum_lambda Pr[b=y+F^T lambda], which equals Pr[(I-GF)^T b=y] since G^T y=0 and FG=I.
